newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index edges up to new high.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index edges up to new high.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average edged higher Monday to set its fifth record of the New Year as late buying helped the market overcome profit-taking in the shares of oil companies.

The 30-stock Dow index rose 5.39 points to 6,709.18, surpassing Friday's record finish of 6,703.79. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,366 to 1,159 on active volume of 443 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The market also was devoid of the volatility that has marked trading since the start of the year.
J.P. Morgan & Co. Inc. was the strongest performer among Dow components, rising 2-3/4 to 102-1/2 after reporting stronger-than-expected fourth quarter earnings.
The bank's results triggered a rally in financial shares, but analysts said activity appeared restrained ahead of Tuesday's release of the consumer price index for December.
Oil stocks, the big winners last week, fell broadly following a sharp drop in crude oil prices.
"When you start profit-taking you have to go where the profits are," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "Clearly the oil shares have been strong performers lately."
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February crude oil lost 90 cents to $25.19 a barrel in a sell-off that was fuelled by forecasts of warmer temperatures in the Northeast.

Elsewhere, the market was noticeably muted and stocks held to fairly tight ranges. The session was the first this year that failed to produce a move of 50 points in the Dow index to trigger the NYSE's programme trading curbs.
"Today was a moment to breathe," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We still saw evidence that profit-taking is short-lived, shallow and greeted with buyers."
Stocks got little help from bonds as the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slipped 2/32 point, leaving its yield unchanged at Friday's close of 6.85 percent, which was up from 6.75 percent on Thursday.
Despite the recent rise in interest rates, some analysts saw reason for optimism.
"What stuck out more than anything were the utilities, where we saw some buying," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.
Because the shares of utilities companies are viewed as a barometer of interest rate sentiment, he said, "We may be getting our first inkling that rates are topping out."
Among financial shares, BankAmerica Corp rose 1-1/4 to 99-1/4 and First Chicago NBD Corp. gained 7/8 to 53-3/8.
In the oil sector, Texaco Inc. shed 1-3/8 to 106, Exxon Corp. slipped 2-5/8 to 103-1/8, and Mobil Corp. dipped 2-1/2 to 127-5/8.
In individual issues, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. gained 1-3/4 to 29-3/8. After the close, Advanced Micro reported a fourth quarter loss vs. a profit a year ago.

Amgen Inc. dipped 2-1/16 to 53, after the company' stock was downgraded by brokerage houses. Last Friday, Amgen and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc. announced disappointing results in a Phase III trial of their drug intended to treat Lou Gehrig's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
Regeneron fell 1-5/8 to 9-3/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 1.11 points to 1,330.91.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 0.01 to 759.51, a record. The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.09 to 586.13.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.05 to 400.71. The average share was unchanged.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,360.047 down 2.679 or 0.04 percent.
